summary: Apollo POC: spec, structure and localization gates wired; baseline frozen

reason: new gates, not new defects — detection widened, so the pre-existing findings were frozen rather than treated as regressions
summary: floor extended to cover G05 structure rules, G06 localization rules and the per-spec fail counts

The gates that found real defects were the ones read out of each repo's own generated source, not the ones translated from another platform. Every wrong number published this week came from a hand-grep rather than from the tool.
Phase 1 module flags gate at isExcluded, the call every page, component and element already makes: 15 of 16 modules switch off with no per-page guard

reason: cmd_baseline did not mirror _check_repo, so every G08 finding read as new forever; X07 (ads has no surface to gate) and X12 (pages that bypass the scaffold) are pre-existing debt, recorded so the count can only fall
summary: G08 rule ids join the ratchet floor

The gate was pointed at the registry instead of the domain and reported clean over 15 unguarded modules (F11). Fixing it exposed the real design: the UIKit already routes every surface through isExcluded(pageId/componentId/elementId), so one lookup there replaces 240 hand-placed guards — and X12 watches the pages that escape it.
module ownership audited against the Phase 1 catalog: notification tray moved to Feed, search to Discovery, cross-module components and per-platform pageId aliases claimed

The catalog was the authority all along and nothing had read it end to end. Four mappings were wrong, ten pageIds only one platform spells were unowned, and the chokepoint's page-owner ?? component-owner meant a component could never outvote its host page. Apollo could not have found any of it — X13 and X14 now enumerate from each platform, and the runtime tests carry the rest.
page-level gate reaches every page on all three platforms: iOS via updateTheme(with:) plus AmityModuleGateView on the 15 pages it misses, Web via an explicit isExcluded return on 57 pages

The chokepoint was only a chokepoint on Android — iOS never asked isExcluded at page level and Web asked in 2 of 60, while X11 reported green because it only checked that the table was consulted. Chasing the last ungated page surfaced F14: a config id in a string literal opened a phantom block comment and the scanner had been reading holes.
third segment of the config id: 57 module-entry elements now belong to their module, so switching one off closes the doors into it as well as emptying its pages

Pages and components disappeared and every button that led to them stayed — a Clips tab on a live home screen, tapping into emptiness. The matrix test was green because it asserted ids from the shared table instead of ids the platform declares, which is the same trap as newsfeed_component one round earlier.
X16: for every owned element, something on the platform must actually consult the gate — five controls were owned, reported clean and never asked about

Three rules asked who owns an id and none asked whether anyone looks the owner up, so five open doors sat behind three zeros. Writing the sensor repeated the mistake: it knew one of iOS's two idioms and credited Web elements to the declaring file rather than the wrapper that renders them, and reported fourteen where the truth was five.
measured the module gate: 1725-2435 ns a call, memoised per config id to 23-35 ns on Android

retired the three hand-written clip guards and the features registry they belonged to — the chokepoint covers clip like the other fifteen, and the leftovers were what made a sixteen-module change read as clip-only
guarantee rules cannot be baselined; every element must be reachable by a gate, not merely named like a door

The gate caught a new ungated page and one run of apollo baseline — the command the CI error suggests — made it permanently silent. Debt and broken guarantees were sharing a floor. Separating them exposed that the element rule was keyed on spelling: create_livestream_shortcut was caught, go_live_now was not, and the name pass had missed communities_button, for_you_button and clip_caption.
sample app gained a Phase 1 module screen: 16 switches, bundle rules shown live, runtime overrides through setFeatureOverrides
iOS and Web sample apps gained the Phase 1 module switches: iOS a page over a public façade on AmityUIKit4Manager, Web a Storybook control plus a panel naming which rule held what off

Presentation and guide were still describing 0.3.0 — five gates, no localization, no record, no module flags. Updated against live numbers pulled from the contract and the tables rather than memory, which caught that the deck's insert anchor had silently missed and my script printed success anyway.
install-skill reaches vise parity (11 targets incl. gemini, four freshness states, --force, doctor reports every copy); setup stops overwriting an explicit registration and says where it looked

Walked the deck's own instructions cold as an attendee with no repo access — the two places a workshop room gets stuck were a clone failure printed detached from its repo and a doctor fix line pointing at the command that had just failed. Then running setup -g to read its output silently re-pointed the Web repo at another branch and the gate blamed the code: a command that guesses must not overwrite what somebody set by hand.
